title: Guard SkippedTasks.build()'s fire-and-forget prefs load with ref.mounted
why: build() kicks off an un-awaited async side effect (SM-2 forbids side effects in build). _loadFromPrefs() then does `await SharedPreferences.getInstance()` and further awaits before writing `state = ...` twice, with no `ref.mounted` check (SM-4) anywhere in the method. If the provider is disposed (e.g. the user navigates off the Scheduler screen quickly) before the load resolves, the post-await `state = ...` throws Riverpod 3's UnmountedRefException — which the surrounding try/catch swallows and logs via `AppLogger.instance.error(event: 'Failed to load skipped tasks', ...)`, i.e. a routine dispose race gets misreported as a genuine load failure in production logs/Crashlytics breadcrumbs, obscuring real failures of the same code path.
recommendation: Check `ref.mounted` immediately before each `state = ...` assignment in _loadFromPrefs, and return early (without logging) when unmounted, matching Riverpod 3's documented SM-4 pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.
acceptance_criteria: _loadFromPrefs checks ref.mounted before both `state = refs.toSet()` and `state = {}`.
A widget test that disposes the ProviderContainer/screen mid-load does not produce an AppLogger error log.
